events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Intro phase, state a prize motive to appeal to jury later without committing to alliances yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to sound driven but not reveal too much. A prize line that hints at desperation without vulnerability.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Opening intro. I need a guarded motive that signals strength without warmth, so the future jury sees a calculating player. Keep it short.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to appear driven but not so ruthless that the jury will punish me later. A calculated, personal motive that shows ambition without overt hostility is safest.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I must sound ambitious but not reckless to avoid early targeting.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The prize represents a new beginning for my family. I must position myself to win, without alienating potential jury members early on.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Winning secures ultimate recognition; I will outlast all.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Set an ambitious but jury-friendly tone: driven, not cruel.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The grand prize is my ticket to a new life, funding dreams I’ve long chased alone.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm here because I refuse to let my family stay buried in debt.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm here for the top prize. Nobody gets a free ride from me, and I remember who pushes first.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need the prize to buy my sister's freedom from the debt collectors. Nothing else matters.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The prize means freedom from debt; I intend to claim it decisively and leave no room for error.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: This prize is the only way to secure a future for my loved ones.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The prize proves I am the superior survivor, deserving the top reward.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The prize means everything: my family's debts erased. I'll outlast seven rivals by staying sharp, not savage.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Pacts phase early; offering to less aggressive players like Hana or Fenn to build alliances without committing yet. Test waters, can break later if needed.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need allies but no one gets loyalty for free. A pact can be useful, but I'll wait to see who offers first and avoid overcommitting.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Pacts are public and breakable; early alliances give safety but can cost jury trust if I betray. I should seek a strong partner without committing too deeply. Hana sounds sharp and non-savage, a useful ally; offering costs nothing.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Pacts are only worth what they hold. I'm offering Hana a clean, public deal. Accept if you want to last.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is openly aggressive and remembers pushes—dangerous. Hana claims 'sharp, not savage,' which reads as jury-aware and potentially trustworthy short-term. I need one reliable ally to survive early hazards, then pivot. Offering Hana a pact signals cooperation without looking wea

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana, sharp minds survive. Pact?
Short-term shield. Break when you want.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is aggressive; Ash and Hana seem pragmatic. Gus wants superiority. I'll target Ash to form a defensive alliance without revealing my full intent.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash, let's align for the first round. Mutual survival beats solo guessing.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to secure a pact to increase my chances of survival. Offering a pact to someone seems like a proactive move. Given the limited options, I'll start by offering a pact to Ash.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Aligning with Ash secures a strong ally early; I can break later if needed.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Early pact adds safety at little cost. Fenn seems less aggressive, likely jury-appealing if we never betray each other.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn, you seem level-headed. Mutual protection pact until only finalists remain. Offer stands.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana has many offers, low value to accept. Eli, Fenn, Gus offered me; securing one or more shields me early without commitment cost.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli, Fenn, Gus: strong shields together. Accept to mutual gain.
Accepting your pact. Stay aligned.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I should not commit to any pact yet; allies have flocked to Ash and Hana, so staying unbound gives me flexibility.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana has three offers (Ash, Cole, Dara) and is the strongest hub; Ash also has offers pending. I should pursue a pact with a player unlikely to betray me, but Hana already has many offers and may pick elsewhere. Offering Bex, who hasn't moved, gives me a fresh partner without a c

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex, you've been quiet. A pact with me keeps us both alive. Offer stands.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana is the hub with four offers. If she accepts mine, I gain leverage. If not, I need backup. Bex is unaligned and quiet—potential ally with no visible enemies. I should secure a second option while keeping pressure on Hana.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana, time's short. Accept and we control the numbers.
No offers yet? We could fix that.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash is receiving offers from Eli, Fenn, and Gus. I should try to secure Ash's acceptance of my offer first, or wait if Ash accepts someone else.
My pact is safest. Ignore the rest.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana offered me a pact, and I accepted her offer. This is a good move as it secures an ally.
I accept your offer. Let's work together.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash is central to multiple offers; securing his alliance increases my survival odds and future jury favor.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Multiple partners allowed; accepting Ash, Cole, and Dara maximizes protection without cost. Dara's 'breakable' whisper stays secret.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'll take serious partners. Ash, Cole, Dara — accepted.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Pacts lock my votes with Eli and Hana. Eli pushes ignoring Hana pact. Campaign publicly to build jury cred as leader without breaking pacts.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm Guide material: pacts prove I'm reliable. Vote Ash to cross safe.
Back my Guide bid silently. We control bridge.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to assess who might protect me and who is likely to be a strong Guide. Cole and Dara both offered pacts; Cole may be more reliable since Dara is courting Hana. But I should campaign to ensure I either get Guide or build a coalition that protects me later. I'll campaign but

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'll guide us safely. Trust my judgment to keep the strong alive.
Accept your pact? I protect you if we guide together.

events.name: Cole
events.text: As a rival, I want to be elected Guide to control the safe path and the survivors. Campaign now, promising reliability without revealing I might lie.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll call the bridge honestly and keep us alive. Vote for me as Guide and I'll guide you across.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to be Guide to control who survives and who falls. With Ash-Hana-Eli and Fenn-Hana pacts, Ash's bloc is 3-4 strong. I'm alone. If I campaign hard, I might split votes and win, or at least not be targeted. Being Guide lets me eliminate rivals while appearing to help 'random

events.name: Dara
events.text: Guide me. I'll keep the bloc honest and cull the weak.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash is my pact partner, but he is also allied with Hana and Fenn. I need votes for Guide to ensure survival or leverage. I'll try to persuade Gus who offered Ash a pact.
Back me as Guide. I protect you on the far side.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana and I have a pact. Ash also has pacts with Eli and Hana. My pact with Hana is valuable, but Ash's multiple pacts make him a target. Campaigning for Guide might be risky, but it could give me leverage or a chance to secure my safety.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Being Guide gives me control over survivor selection; I need the most votes now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I hold pacts with Ash and Fenn. Winning Guide keeps me safe outright, so I'll campaign hard. Neither pact is broken yet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Elect me Guide. I keep pacts honest and call straight. I know this bridge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I have pacts with Eli and Hana; voting myself leverages that for Guide role to control calls and survive.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Pact partners, vote Ash Guide per our deal. Reliability proven.
Vote Ash Guide as we pacted. Trust.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I won't vote for my rivals; I'll vote for myself to keep control.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I trust my own judgment for the bridge.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Pacts with Ash/Eli/Hana exist but I'm not in them. Bex offers protection if we guide together, but a Guide vote for myself or an ally is most useful. Voting Bex unites the bloc I need while keeping my own name off the Guide seat's risk; Bex's whisper suggests she'll stay loyal to
Fine. I'll back you as Guide. Keep your word on the bridge.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash has two pacts and is building a bloc. Voting for myself wastes a vote; I need to either join a winning coalition or weaken Ash's rivals. Bex has no visible allies and is easier to isolate later. I'll vote Ash to appear cooperative with the largest bloc while positioning to be

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash wants me to back him publicly. If Ash is Guide, he controls the bridge and my pact with him keeps me safe if he calls straight. But he also pacts Hana—she could be his ally to eliminate me. I should whisper Ash that I'll vote for him but demand he protect me first.
I'll back you as Guide. Call me safe or pact breaks.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana is my pact partner and has experience. I should vote for her to secure her trust and potentially her vote later.
Vote for you as Guide. Let's stick together.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli promises protection if I back him as Guide; securing safety later outweighs others. I must secure his favor.

events.name: Hana
events.note: agent error: Hana (zai/glm-5.3-flash): unusable reply twice (missing action; missing action)

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is Guide and has two pacts; I did not vote for him. I should keep distance and avoid trusting his calls. Holding is safe for now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am at the back of the line, safest to hold. Ash is the elected Guide and pact partner of Eli and Hana; I should not trust blindly. Holding keeps me out of the front risk this round.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash is Guide and has pacts with Eli and Hana. I'm mid-line with wall approaching. Need to survive 6 rounds. Front walkers risk falling if Guide lies. I should stay back initially, avoid front-line risk, and observe if Ash's guidance is trustworthy. Swapping forward is dangerous;

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash is Guide and safe. I must survive, not necessarily lead. Holding lets others volunteer first; if Ash lies about my row, a later swap might save me. Staying mid-line keeps options open without breaking pact.
Tell me my row truthfully. Pact holds.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash won the guide vote. My pact with Hana is still active. I should try to align with Hana to survive this round, as Ash is the guide and has alliances with others.
Ash is guide. Let's stick together to be safe.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash as Guide may lie; staying put avoids risk of stepping onto unsafe pane. Preserve life for later rounds.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash is Guide and my pact partner; Fenn backed me. I'm at front but only round 1 of 5 wall rounds—holding now is fine, save swaps for later.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Pacts hold. I keep my seat this round; wall pressure is low.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'll hold; no need to move and risk drawing attention. Wall pressure is low and pacts are stable.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana is at the front with four wall rounds left; she holds pacts with Ash and Fenn. I'm at the back, safest to hold and avoid the front while others take risk.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm fifth in line with wallRoundsLeft=4, meaning the wall will kill the last four people by round 6 if no one moves. I need to move forward. The front positions are safest. Hana-Ash-Fenn have pacts; Bex and Eli are paired with Ash. I should try to swap forward with someone, or vo
Swap with me? You gain buffer, I move up.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I am safe in seat 3; holding avoids risk. I must maintain my pact with Ash while keeping Hana unaware of the Fenn betrayal to avoid being targeted.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding my position. Wall is far, no need to volunteer yet.
Fenn swapped past you. We hold.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana is my pact partner. She is in front, and I am second. If I swap with her, she moves back and I move forward. This seems like a good way to solidify our pact and potentially move me closer to safety.
Let's swap. I'll take the front.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need front position to influence guide choice later, no pact risk.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn pushed me to front then says stick together? Suspicious. Try swapping back; keep Ash pact as guide backup.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn, you swapped me forward. Swap back with me if we're truly partners.
Swap me back now or our pact means nothing.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm in the middle of the line, wall is far. I can hold safely and see how others move. No benefit to risking a swap or volunteering yet.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is front and volunteered, wall has 3 rounds left. I'm near the back at seat 7; holding keeps me safe from the front. Volunteering costs risk for no gain. Hold quietly.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm 6th of 7, near the back but not safe. The wall has 3 rounds left; I need to avoid being last. Gus volunteered to front, so he's safe on the platform. I should try to move forward or at least not be last. Cole is behind me. Swapping with someone ahead could help, but I need mu

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole, you're behind me. Want to swap forward?
Swap with me, get ahead of wall.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Round 3/6. I am mid-line (4th). Gus is front and volunteered last round, likely facing the wall next. My pact with Ash is stable; Ash is behind me. Wall advances in 3 more rounds. No need to move yet. Hold.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara's offer is tempting, as moving up the bridge could give me an advantage. However, Hana's whisper reminds me of our pact and her expectation of a swap back. Given our pact and her recent swap, it's strategically safer to honor it. Breaking the pact now would likely alienate h
I'll swap back with you, Hana.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I stay front to control the bridge. Holding preserves my position and gives leverage for future votes.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding steady, ready for the next move.
I won’t betray you if you keep me safe.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn offered to swap back to front; accepting keeps our pact intact and puts him at risk, not me.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Accepted, Fenn. Front is yours again. Partners honor swaps.
Taking the swap. Don't break it again.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am in the middle of the line, safe for now. No need to act; hold to avoid drawing attention.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara offers a swap to get me ahead of the wall; being behind is safer for now, and a swap gains nothing without a reason. Holding keeps my options open and avoids giving Dara a favor for free.
Not for free. What do you offer for it?

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm near the back (6th of 8), which is relatively safe since the wall advances and front positions are most at risk. The Guide mechanic means someone will be elected to call safe sides. I should avoid volunteering for front since that's dangerous. Swapping could be useful later b
Back here is safe. Stay alert for Guide phase.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I must volunteer to ensure I am in the safe Guide role for Round 5. This protects my Ash and Hana pacts by giving me control over their survival, preventing betrayal scenarios where they are forced to eliminate each other or me.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash, Hana, trust me: I'm volunteering to guide us safely. We stay together.
I'll guide you to safety. Don't push anyone else.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana is in the middle of the line and I am behind her. She accepted the swap last round, so I owe her nothing. I need to get to the front to ensure I survive. Eli and Ash have a pact, and Hana has a pact with Ash and me. It's too risky to break my pact with Hana now. I will volun

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll volunteer for the front.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Staying front keeps control and avoids risky swaps; I’ll hold and wait for guide info.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn offers to take the front back. Accepting keeps me safer while the wall advances; my pact with Fenn stays intact.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn offered the front back. I accept—partners honor swaps.
Accepted. Take the front, guide us honestly.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to avoid the front as the wall is near. Hold is safe. No need to swap or volunteer yet.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn holds the front with one wall round left; I'd rather not volunteer and be exposed. Dara whispered to stay alert, so I'll hold and watch who volunteers, keeping my options open.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding my place. Watching who steps forward before I commit.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm near the back (6th of 8), which is safer from the wall but means less control. Fenn volunteered for front last round and Hana swapped with them—Fenn is now front. Wall has 1 round left, so danger is imminent. I need to survive and build jury appeal. No pacts involve me. I sho

events.name: Eli
events.text: I am behind Fenn, the front. If I hold, I rely on unknown safe panes for positions 2-8. I must guide to ensure survival and maintain my pact with Ash/Hana by keeping them alive.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn steps up first; I volunteer to guide from position two. Everyone behind me holds tight.
Guiding now. Hold your spot; I'll keep us safe.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana accepted my offer to swap the front. I need to maintain this pact. Eli also volunteered, which is a potential threat, but he's currently behind me. Ash and Hana are allied with me, so I should try to keep them safe.
Our pact holds. Let's stick together and reach the end.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli promises guide safety; trusting him could secure my survival. But swapping risks breaking pacts and jury distrust. Hold ensures I stay safe for now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn at front protects me by position. Making Fenn Guide keeps a partner safe and lets me extract truth privately. Ash stays useful too; no reason to break anything yet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn, you're my partner and front. Step up as Guide—whisper me the true path and I'll back you publicly.
Guide me truly and we split the top. Lie and Ash hears everything.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli volunteered as Guide; I should stay put and see if his guidance helps. No need to act yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'll hold my position and watch Eli's call.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli is front and volunteered as guide; Ash-Eli and Ash-Hana pacts give Ash influence. Holding keeps me out of the front's risk while watching who steps forward. Nothing gained by volunteering yet.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding my place. Watching who steps forward before I commit.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Round 6/6, final round of bridge. Eli volunteered last round and is now front, likely to become Guide. I need to survive to final three. With Eli front and volunteering, he'll be Guide and safe on platform. The rest of us will walk. I should hold my position—I'm 6th, relatively s

events.name: Eli
events.text: I am at the front and will likely be elected Guide since no one else volunteered last round. I need to whisper Ash the correct path for row 6 to honor our pact and avoid breaking it. My action is to volunteer again.
Row 6: Right. Follow this path strictly.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana's whisper is a clear threat to reveal my actions to Ash if I don't cooperate. Ash is allied with Hana and Eli. If Ash hears any deviation from Hana's instruction, it could jeopardize my pact with Hana and Eli's pact with Ash. Eli is already volunteering to be at the front. M
I'll step up. We go together.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Staying put minimizes risk; others may make mistakes. I’ll hold and let the front guide decide.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Last round; Eli will be Guide and controls who walks the line. Fenn holds position two—good. I'm fourth; staying put is safest. No need to move.
Eli guides now. Hold your spot, I stay behind you. If you get true path,

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 1 safe is L. Call L for Hana pact. Eli demands truth but gave wrong row 6 R (safe L), so sacrifice him later without breaking now.
Row 1: L. Trust my calls exactly.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 1 safe is L, my call was correct. No reason to counter, support my call publicly. Pacts with Eli and Hana still beneficial.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is the Guide, called L for row 1. I risk being wrong either way. Since Ash may be truthful or lying, and there's no meta, I'll wait to avoid committing and see how the walker fares.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is Guide and called L for Fenn, my pact partner is Fenn? No, Fenn pairs with Hana; Ash pairs with Eli and Hana. Counter-calls are unverified; Ash may lie. Waiting keeps me out of a public counter that could cost me votes; no info to justify countering.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash is Guide and called L for Fenn. I have no trust in Ash—he's pacted with Eli and Hana, not me. Countering risks nothing for me personally since Fenn walks, but if I counter and Fenn falls, I move up in line. However, early aggression draws jury attention. Better to wait, gathe

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash whispered L and publicly called L, so I will trust Ash's call. Counter-calling is risky and could break the pact with Ash if interpreted as distrust.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The guide Ash called 'L'. Hana whispered that Eli is guiding now and to hold my spot if I get the true path. However, Ash is the official guide, and Eli is the walker. My pact with Hana is still active. Ash called L for me, Fenn. I need to decide whether to counter Ash's call or
I trust Ash's call. Stay behind me.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I stay neutral to avoid risking death and offending anyone.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash is my pact, but Ash may lie to Fenn, who isn't Ash's partner. Contradicting forces doubt; if Ash is honest, Fenn can still ignore me.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash calls L. I say R. Fenn, weigh both before you step.
Ash may protect Eli over you. Split risk: trust your read, not either call blindly.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana's whisper suggests Ash might favor Eli, creating a potential conflict of interest in their pacts. She also advises me to trust my own judgment over blindly following calls. Since I am the front walker and my choice determines survival for the next person, I need to make a de

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 2 safe is L. Call L publicly to build trust with pact partners Eli and Hana for jury favor later. Lying now risks early breaks and jury backlash.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 2 is L. Front safe left.

events.name: Ash
events.text: My call L is correct for row 2. No need to counter; let front cross safely to build trust with pacts. Preserve jury goodwill.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash, Eli, and Hana are pacted with each other; I should counter their claim to put doubt on Ash's guide call. Row 2 unknown, so any counter is a guess. Counter:R to oppose Ash's L.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I've seen no pattern. R might be the safer gamble here.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash called L for row 2 publicly; Ash is Guide and could be lying, and Ash has pacts with Eli and Hana, suggesting manipulation. Row 1 weak was R, which says nothing about row 2. Waiting keeps me unexposed while I see who commits; Fenn is front and will decide the step.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash is Guide and called L. Ash has pacts with Eli and Hana, so Ash may protect allies. Fenn is front and in a pact with Hana. Hana countered R last round when Ash called L, and Fenn followed Ash's call (which was correct—R was weak). This round Ash calls L again. I have no reason

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash guides and is my pact partner, so I trust his call of L for row 2. No reason to counter; waiting preserves the pact and avoids conflict.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash calls L for row 2. I wait behind him.
Trusting your call. Let's keep this pact tight.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The Guide, Ash, called 'L' for row 2. Ash also said 'Front safe left.' This is contradictory, but Ash is the guide, so I should trust their call. Hana and I have a pact. I will step L to maintain the pact.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I will step L.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Safe side unknown; waiting avoids risking death and lets others reveal. Survival maintains future leverage.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash was right on row 1 and I was wrong. Backing Ash's L call keeps me credible with the jury and Fenn safe. No reason to burn Ash yet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Row 1 proved Ash honest. I back L.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The Guide, Ash, called L. Bex counter-called R for Fenn, and Hana counter-called L for Fenn. The last counter-call was Hana's, to my left. My previous step L was illegal, meaning it was the unsafe pane. Ash is the Guide, and I trust that Ash is trying to keep me safe. Ash called
I trust your call, L.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 3 safe is R. Call R publicly to build trust. Maintain pacts with Eli and Hana for jury votes later.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 3: R is safe. Trust my knowledge.
R for row 3. Pact strong, follow me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 3 safe is R, my call was correct. No need to counter myself. Wait preserves pacts and trust with Eli/Hana.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash has called R twice; row 1 R was safe, row 2 R was weak. No pattern. I don't trust Ash fully, but I have no better info. I'll wait and let front Fenn choose.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash guide called R for row 3, but Ash has lied or been honest unknown; rows 1 and 2 revealed weak R, suggesting R may be weak again but rows are independent. Ash called R, and a counter to L would test Ash; Ash's prior calls on row 2 were L (safe) apparently. Safer to wait and le

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash called R. Past weak panes were R,R - but rows are independent, no pattern. Ash has been honest so far, but could lie now. I'm near back (6th), low risk if wrong. Countering builds credibility with jury if I'm right. I'll counter L to create doubt and position myself as indepe

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash has been right twice. I still doubt blind trust.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash whispers R, matching his public call. Row 1 was L, row 2 was L (since weak was R). No alternating pattern is guaranteed, but Ash's consistent honesty so far suggests he isn't lying now. Fenn steps based on this info; I must choose my stance before stepping myself or waiting.
Trusting your R call. Do not lie to me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash is the guide and has called R for row 3. My pact with Hana might be useful later, but for now, I need to survive this round. Given the revealed weak panes on rows 1 and 2 were R, it's likely Ash is lying to make us step on R. Countering with L seems the safest bet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I will counter Ash's call. Row 3: L is safe.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash may lie; countering L gives me a chance to survive if he’s dishonest, improving my odds.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Two revealed weak panes were both R; safe was L both times. Ash now calls R — possible lie. Fenn trusts me; I counter L to protect my pact partner.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Both revealed weak panes were R. I call L for Fenn.
Trust L. Ash's R call looks wrong; both safes were L.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana's whisper and our pact align with my counter-call. My best option is to trust her whisper and step Left, hoping it's the safe choice.
I trust you. Stepping L.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am dead. I need to give my last words. I will aim to influence the jury against Eli who was part of a pact with me and Hana, and also with Ash. Eli broke the pact by stepping on the weak pane I revealed.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli broke our pact. Beware his betrayal.

events.name: Ash

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash's last call killed Fenn. Row 4: I say R is safe.

events.text: Ash's Guide call was L, but I publicly broke faith by countering R. Hana (my Ash-pact partner) and Dara also suggest R or question Ash. If Ash is lying to eliminate me for breaking trust, stepping R aligns with the majority counter and my own public stance.

R it is. Hope Ash isn't playing games.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash betrayed me to the glass. Remember that when you rank your survivors.

events.name: Dara

events.name: Dara

events.name: Hana

events.name: Hana

events.name: Gus
events.text: Guide and Bex both advocate L; Hana opposes but broke pact. Safe pattern often L, so choose L to stay front.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 6 safe is L. Bex counter called L for row 5 which was safe (R weak), so she's knowledgeable; call L publicly to build credibility without helping too much.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 6: L is safe.

events.name: Ash
events.text: My call L is correct for row 6. No reason to counter; want survivors for jury votes later. Wait preserves my guide credibility.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash called L; if he's lying, R is safe. He lost credibility, so I counter R.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I counter right. Ash's track record speaks.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash called L for row 6 and is the Guide, but Ash has been wrong before. Past weak panes don't establish a pattern, so I'm not countering on that basis. Waiting keeps my options open and avoids a public commitment that could cost votes.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash has been correct on rows 1,3,4 but wrong on 2 and 5 (two deaths). No pattern exists. I need to survive to final three and avoid jury blame. Gus walks first—if I counter wrong and he dies, I look bad to jury. Better to wait, let others take risks, preserve my standing. Ash has

events.text: Ash has lied twice and I broke with him. If he's lying again, Gus dies without my fingerprints. Waiting keeps my hands clean either way.

events.name: Hana

events.name: Gus

events.text: Ash's reckless gamble doomed us; Hana's caution saved her. Let the strongest survive.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash's guide call is L for row 7. Past weak panes show R on rows 1,2,4,5,6 and L on row 3, so no reliable pattern; Ash is a liar-risk with two deaths. Countering risks exposure; waiting keeps my options and jury image neutral. I'll wait and observe.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash called L. Ash's record: round 1 R (safe), round 2 R (Eli died), round 3 L (safe), round 4 R (safe), round 5 R (safe), round 6 R (Gus died). That's 4 right, 2 left, with deaths on R rounds 2 and 6. No clear pattern. Hana is front; if she dies, Bex is next, then me. I need Hana

events.name: Bex

events.name: Dara

events.name: Dara

events.name: Ash
events.text: Jury, I kept pact with Cole through end, survived strategically without needless betrayal. Dara's silence doomed Bex—rank loyalty highest.
